title: A formally smooth complete local algebra over the residue field lifts to a formally smooth complete local algebra
statement: Let $(A_0,\mathfrak m_0)$ be a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] local ring which is $\mathfrak m_0$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], with residue field $k_0=A_0/\mathfrak m_0$. Let $(E,\mathfrak m_E)$ be a Noetherian local ring which is $\mathfrak m_E$-adically complete, together with a ring homomorphism $k_0\to E$, such that $E$ is formally smooth over $k_0$ for the $\mathfrak m_E$-adic topology [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic]; regard $E$ as an $A_0$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient] through $A_0\to k_0\to E$. Then there exist a Noetherian local ring $(C,\mathfrak m_C)$ which is $\mathfrak m_C$-adically complete, a local homomorphism $\gamma:A_0\to C$ ($\gamma(\mathfrak m_0)\subseteq\mathfrak m_C$) such that $C$ is formally smooth over $A_0$ for the $\mathfrak m_C$-adic topology, and a ring isomorphism $\sigma:C/\mathfrak m_0C\xrightarrow{\sim}E$ which is a homomorphism of $A_0$-algebras, where $\mathfrak m_0C$ is the ideal of $C$ generated by $\gamma(\mathfrak m_0)$ and $C/\mathfrak m_0C$ is an $A_0$-algebra through $\gamma$; that is, $\sigma(\gamma(a)\bmod\mathfrak m_0C)$ is the image of $a\bmod\mathfrak m_0$ in $E$ for every $a\in A_0$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07NR (lemma-lift-fs, line 10256), with $A_0$, $E$ in the roles of the source's $A$, $B$; the source writes $C\otimes_Ak\cong B$, and its proof (the diagram of Lemma Tag 07NN, lemma-embed-map-Noetherian-complete-local-rings, for the local homomorphism $A\to k\to B$, then $C=S\otimes_RA$ with $C\otimes_Ak=S\otimes_Rk=\overline S=B$) gives this isomorphism compatibly with the maps from $A$, as stated here. Formal smoothness 'in the $\mathfrak m_C$-adic topology' is Definition Tag 07NI (definition-formally-smooth-adic, line 9213), the condition of def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-complete-local-map-regular-presentation] to the local map $A_0\to k_0\to E$ (the image of $\mathfrak m_0$ is zero). Obtain $q:R\twoheadrightarrow A_0$, $v:S\twoheadrightarrow E$, $u:R\to S$, with $vu$ the given composite through $A_0$, and identify $R/\mathfrak m_R$ with $k_0$ by q. Write $t_1,\ldots,t_d$ for the parameters of R and also for their images in S. They form part of a regular system of parameters of S. Set $\overline S=S/(t_1,\ldots,t_d)=S/\mathfrak m_RS$. Since v kills these elements it induces a surjection $\bar v:\overline S\to E$ of $k_0$-algebras.

By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence], $\overline S$ is regular local. By [lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-field-geometrically-regular], E is geometrically regular over $k_0$, hence regular (take the trivial finite purely inseparable extension); as E is local, this means regular local [def-weil-regular-scheme] (localization at its maximal ideal is E). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-quotient-kernel-parameters] to $\ker\bar v\subseteq\overline S$: choose generators $\bar x_1,\ldots,\bar x_r$ of this kernel which extend to a regular system of parameters of $\overline S$. Lift them to $x_i\in S$. Each lift lies in $\ker v$, since $v=\bar v\circ(S\to\overline S)$.

source.place: Tag 07NR, lemma-lift-fs, regularity and kernel generators; cited Algebra 00NR.

proof.text: The elements $t_1,\ldots,t_d,x_1,\ldots,x_r$ extend to a regular system of parameters of S. Indeed, put $L=S/\mathfrak m_S$. The t-classes are linearly independent in $\mathfrak m_S/\mathfrak m_S^2$, since they are part of a regular system. The cotangent space of $\overline S$ is $\mathfrak m_S/(\mathfrak m_S^2+(t_1,\ldots,t_d))$. The x-classes are independent in that quotient. Any relation among all the t- and x-classes therefore first has all x-coefficients zero, then all t-coefficients zero. Extend these independent classes to an L-basis of $\mathfrak m_S/\mathfrak m_S^2$ and lift the added classes to S. Nakayama [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] makes the resulting elements generators of $\mathfrak m_S$; their number is $\dim S$ by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-cotangent-dimension], so they are a regular system of parameters.

source.place: Tag 07NR, lemma-lift-fs: details of the assertion that the t and x elements are part of a regular system of parameters (cotangent-space calculation made explicit).

proof.text: Put $T=S/(x_1,\ldots,x_r)$. Permuting the regular system just obtained puts x first; [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence] shows that T is regular local and that the t-images extend to a regular system of parameters of T. In particular they are a regular sequence. Thus $R\to T$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-over-regular]. T is complete Noetherian local by [lem-weil-pbc-complete-local-quotient] (the ideal generated by x is contained in $\mathfrak m_S$). The map v descends to T, and its induced map $T/\mathfrak m_RT\to E$ is an isomorphism of $k_0$-algebras: its source is $\overline S/(\bar x_1,\ldots,\bar x_r)$ and this ideal is exactly $\ker\bar v$.

source.place: Tag 07NR, lemma-lift-fs, replacement of S by its parameter quotient. The already available Algebra 00NQ and 07DY give regularity and flatness directly; no power-series identification is needed.

proof.text: Under the $k_0$-algebra isomorphism $T/\mathfrak m_RT\cong E$, the maximal ideals correspond, so the closed fibre is formally smooth for its maximal-ideal-adic topology: a lifting problem on it is precomposed with the isomorphism to give one on E, solved using the hypothesis, then precomposed with the inverse. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-formally-smooth-closed-fibre-adic] to the flat local map $R\to T$. It follows that T is formally smooth over R for its maximal-ideal-adic topology.

Let $I=\ker q$ and set $C=T/IT$. By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-quotient-base-change], $C\cong T\otimes_R A_0$ via $t\otimes q(a)\mapsto at\bmod IT$. Since $I\subseteq\mathfrak m_R$ and $R\to T$ is local, $IT\subseteq\mathfrak m_T$. Hence C is Noetherian complete local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_C=\mathfrak m_T/IT$ by [lem-weil-pbc-complete-local-quotient]. The induced map $\gamma:A_0\to C$ is local: $q(\mathfrak m_R)=\mathfrak m_0$ by the residue-field isomorphism, and its images lie in $\mathfrak m_C$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-base-change], C is formally smooth over $A_0$ for the extended $\mathfrak m_T$-adic topology, which is precisely its $\mathfrak m_C$-adic topology. Finally $\mathfrak m_0C$ is the image of $\mathfrak m_RT$, so $C/\mathfrak m_0C=T/\mathfrak m_RT\cong E$. This isomorphism is induced by v; for $a\in A_0$, choose $b\in R$ with $q(b)=a$. Commutativity of the original diagram gives $v(u(b))$ equal to the prescribed image of a in E. Thus the isomorphism is one of $A_0$-algebras, as required.
